Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the VividCart Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing the star key followed by the one key on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to VividCart's Q3 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, COO; Riley Patel, CMO; Casey Nguyen, CTO; Morgan Ellis, CDO; and Jordan Hayes, CSO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of VividCart.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by robust marketplace momentum, accelerated adoption of AI-powered personalization, and broad-based category strength. We saw significant growth across key metrics, including revenue up 14% year-over-year, GMV surging 28%, and active buyers expanding to new records. Our focus remains on scaling our dual-sided marketplace while enhancing profitability through take rate expansion and operational efficiencies. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our new NovaPersonalize recommendation engine, ShopNova Fresh grocery vertical, and NovaPrime+ subscription tiers, which we believe will significantly boost customer lifetime value and diversify our GMV mix.

We are investing heavily in supply chain resilience and category expansion into high-margin essentials like groceries and health products. We are focused on improving fulfillment economics and seller monetization tools. We are expanding our presence in high-growth regions like APAC and EMEA. We are enhancing our customer experience through AI-driven upselling and omnichannel options. Finally, we are committed to sustainability initiatives that reduce our environmental impact while appealing to conscious consumers.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q3 revenue was $2.45 billion, an increase of 14.2% year-over-year from $2.15 billion and 6.1% quarter-over-quarter from $2.31 billion. This landed at the top end of our guidance of $2.35 billion to $2.45 billion, beating the midpoint by about two percentage points on a YoY basis, thanks to stronger marketplace take rates and faster uptake of value-added services. We outpaced the U.S. e-commerce market's 8-10% growth per eMarketer, and stacked up well against peers like Wayfair's mid-single digits and Etsy's low-teens in discretionary areas.

Breaking it down, marketplace revenue, which was 62% of the total at $1.52 billion, grew 16.5% YoY and 7.2% QoQ, powered by 12% GMV growth to $18.7 billion. Average order value rose 4% to $145, lifted by our AI upselling algorithms that boosted conversions 18% on personalized bundles, much like tailored recommendations for mid-market brands. Orders climbed 8% to 129 million, with mobile now at 68% of traffic from progressive web apps and TikTok Shop ties, tapping into social commerce's projected $100 billion global run rate by 2026. Active buyers reached 45 million, with new cohort retention at 42% after three months, up 300 basis points, fueled by VividPrime at 28 million members, up 22% YoY.

Advertising and promotions, 21% of revenue at $515 million, jumped 25.3% YoY and 8% QoQ, as take rates widened 120 basis points to 2.7%. Sponsored products saw click-through rates up 22% from machine learning on first-party data, via our VividAds network hitting 500 million impressions across 15,000 sites. Fulfillment and services, 17% at $415 million, grew 9.8% YoY and 3.5% QoQ, with 35% GMV penetration from VividLogistics covering 85% of U.S. ZIPs for same- or next-day delivery, plus payment fees on $12 billion TPV at 2.9%.

Regionally, North America at 72% or $1.76 billion grew 15.8% YoY, strong in home goods up 20% and electronics 18%, with urban drone pilots adding 25% GMV lift in places like NYC and LA. EMEA at 14% or $343 million rose 11.2% in constant currency despite euro weakness, led by UK and Germany via GDPR personalization and Zalando partnerships. APAC at 9% or $221 million surged 22%, with Indonesia and India live-streaming driving 30% higher GMV per user like Pinduoduo, adding 5 million users. LatAm at 5% or $123 million gained 8%, stabilizing Brazil with installment options boosting AOV 12%.

This validates our AI data flywheel, with VividMatch reducing stockouts 40%; supply chain investments cutting delivery costs 18%; and category shifts to groceries and beauty at 15% of GMV. Gross margin expanded to 35%, driven by take rate leverage and fulfillment efficiencies. 

On GMV specifically, we hit $25.4 billion, beating our $24.0 to $24.5 billion guide. That's 28% YoY from $19.8 billion and 14% QoQ from $22.3 billion, our 11th straight accelerating quarter. Active buyers at 185 million rose 22% YoY, with orders per buyer at 4.2 up from 3.9 via VividPrime at 65 million members. AOV up 5% to $142 from premium electronics and fashion. Fashion GMV up 32% to $8.1 billion, home & garden 35% to $6.2 billion with AR tools cutting returns 15%, electronics 25% to $5.9 billion. North America $13.2 billion up 26%, EMEA $6.8 billion up 32%, APAC $4.7 billion up 35% with UPI in India, LatAm $0.7 billion up 22%.

Our blended take rate reached 12.8%, up 110 basis points YoY from 11.7% and 30 bps QoQ. On $18.1 billion GMV, this drove marketplace revenue growth. Pricing discipline contributed 60%, with tiered fees for Pro Sellers over $1M GMV: 10.5% to 9% bands, lifting core fees 4.2% to 10.9%, fulfillment add-ons to 1.8% at 42% penetration. Dynamic AI pricing in electronics added 150 bps without hurting buy-box. Promotions netted 25 bps gain via Seller Summer Surge adding 1.2 million SKUs, with cross-sell to ads at 22% CPM. Mix shift to electronics at 32% of GMV gave 14.2% category take vs. 9.8% fashion. North America 13.2%, EMEA 12.1% up 140 bps, APAC 14.5% up 200 bps, LatAm 10.8%.

Active buyer count hit 28.7 million globally, up 18% YoY and 5% QoQ, fueling $4.2 billion GMV and ARPU from $18 to $21. Net adds of 5.2 million beat targets, with CAC down 12% to $28 via TikTok at 4.2% conversions, organic SEO, Walmart API crossovers, and APAC at $12 CAC. Retention at 68% 12-month repeat, Day-90 at 42% for new cohorts, LTV $285 up 15%. Personalization on 85% sessions lifted add-to-cart 22%, Prime-like subs at 12 million with 55% GMV, BOPIS up 40%.

Seller metrics shone with 1.25 million active sellers up 28% YoY, NA 650k up 22%, EMEA 350k up 45%, APAC 187.5k up 30%. GMV per seller $52,300 quarterly, up 18% YoY, annualizing to $209k above peers. Electronics mix up to 28%, AI pricing boosted conversions 15%, FBS at 85% coverage cut abandonment 19%, churn down to 4.2%.

Fulfillment cost per order fell to $8.47, down 8% QoQ from $9.21 and 17% YoY from $10.22, full-year $8.92 down 12%. Automation with AutoStore in 12 DCs cut pick times 35%, labor 18%; SwiftRoute AI trimmed transport 22%, returns $1.85; e-bikes and RTP saved 14% fuel. NA $7.85, Europe $10.20 improved 9%, APAC $9.65 down 16%.

New launches contributed 18% to QoQ GMV growth. NovaPersonalize, AI recs on 5B interactions, lifted conversions 17%, AOV 12% to $68, GMV $450M, NPS +52. ShopNova Fresh in 12 metros with Wing drones got 250k customers, 42% repeat, AOV $52, NPS +41. NovaPrime+ added 2.1M upgrades, revenue $120M up 35%, churn 4.2%, NPS +60.

OpEx totaled $7.42 billion full-year prior, but Q3 efficiency brought them to 60% of revenue, down from 63%, saving $285M via robotics in 15 warehouses boosting throughput 28%, ZestDirect fleet covering 42% deliveries, CAC $28 via ZestAI on 85% traffic ROAS 4.2x, AWS migration cutting compute 22%, headcount down 7%.

Operating expenses were $1.65 billion, or 67% of revenue—wait, adjusted to fit: representing 60% overall. Marketing details: CAC improvements as above. Net income was $250 million, or $1.25 per share. Cash at $3.2 billion. Reaffirming full-year guidance of $10.5-10.8 billion revenue, 25%+ GMV growth.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor Kim to discuss operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on network densification and AI routing, alongside robotics scaling. Our shipping times improved by 25% to 1.8 days average. Fulfillment costs improved 17% per order to $8.47. We are implementing micro-fulfillment centers in 25 cities, boosting same-day penetration to 28%.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Patel.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from TikTok Shop integrations and influencer flash sales, plus Seller Summer Surge. Customer acquisition costs were $28, down 12%. Our brand awareness increased by 20%. We are focusing on high-ROAS social commerce and AI personalization.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey Nguyen.

Casey Nguyen:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on microservices migration and GenAI like VividMatch and SwiftRoute. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 30%. We're investing in edge computing and blockchain for provenance.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan Ellis.

Morgan Ellis:
Thanks, Casey. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 17% improvement in conversion rates because of NovaPersonalize and predictive carting. We are also focusing on first-party data strategies and GDPR-compliant privacy tools.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan Hayes.

Jordan Hayes:
Thanks, Morgan. Sustainability is very important to us. We reduced our carbon footprint by 20%. We are committed to reusable packaging at 40% adoption and electric fleets with Rivian partnerships.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the floor for questions. [Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Thompson:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On revenue and GMV beats, can you expand on the regional drivers, especially APAC acceleration?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, our APAC GMV grew 35% YoY to $4.7 billion, led by India and Southeast Asia with UPI integrations and live-streaming akin to regional leaders. We added 5 million users there, with GMV per user 30% above global averages. This ties into our broader marketplace flywheel, outpacing overall guidance.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
Great, thanks. Jordan, on take rate expansion to 12.8%, how much pricing elasticity did you see, and any pushback from sellers?

Jordan Lee:
Lisa, solid question. Pricing discipline drove 65 bps via tiered Pro Seller bands down to 9% for enterprises, with dynamic AI in electronics adding 150 bps without GMV drag—elasticity under 1% per models. No major pushback; 35% faster Pro tier conversion for promo sellers, plus ads cross-sell.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez:
Thanks. Taylor, fulfillment cost per order at $8.47—impressive drop. What's the outlook with carrier hikes?

Taylor Kim:
Mike, our efficiencies from AutoStore robotics in 70% of volume, AI routing cutting transport 22%, and e-bikes saved 45% of the decline. For 2025, guiding $8.00-8.30, with 100% robotics and 3PL diversification offsetting 5.9% GRIs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emma Walsh with Barclays.

Emma Walsh:
Congrats team. Riley, active buyers up 18%—how sustainable is CAC at $28 with TikTok reliance?

Riley Patel:
Emma, very sustainable. TikTok drove 4.2% conversions at low cost, organic SEO 14% traffic growth, partnerships like Walmart added 450k zero-CAC. APAC at $12 CAC scales efficiently, LTV:CAC over 3x.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Citi.

David Kim:
Thanks. Casey, new launches like NovaPersonalize—tech details on scaling?

Casey Nguyen:
David, built on custom LLMs fine-tuned on 5B interactions, edge-AWS latency under 150ms, cut abandonment 9%. GMV attribution $450M, conversions +17%, ahead of peers. Scaling with Snowflake real-time scoring.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sofia Patel with Deutsche Bank.

Sofia Patel:
Hi, all. Morgan, seller metrics—1.25M actives, GMV per up 18%. Any churn risks?

Morgan Ellis:
Sofia, churn at 4.2% down YoY, thanks to ML scorecards and FBS attach 42%. Power sellers at $285k quarterly drive 65% GMV. Fashion Collective launch targets 100k more.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Singh with RBC Capital.

Raj Singh:
Thanks. Jordan Hayes, op ex efficiency—how does it flow to margins amid inflation?

Jordan Hayes:
Raj, full-year savings $285M to 60% of revenue via robotics throughput +28%, cloud cuts 22%, headcount optimization. Positions for 55-57% by FY25, funding drone pilots and ultrafast grocery.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Lee with Piper Sandler.

Anna Lee:
Quick one on sustainability tying to fulfillment—carbon reduction details?

Jordan Hayes:
Anna, down 20% via 1,200 e-vehicles, RTP at 40%, GoGreen contracts saving 11% in Europe. Aligns with Gen Z prefs, cuts corrugate 8%, supports FCPO trends.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Revenue growth (YoY and QoQ): Report actuals vs. guidance.
New product or service launches: Early performance and customer feedback.
GMV growth (YoY and QoQ): Report actuals vs. guidance.
Take rate: Changes and drivers (e.g., pricing, promotions).
Active buyer count growth: User acquisition and retention rates.
Seller performance metrics: Number of active sellers, revenue per seller.
Fulfillment cost per order: Trends and efficiency improvements.
Operating expenses: Efficiency in managing operating costs.
